Subject: Follow-up: Procurement path & PO details (ACME)

Hi Samantha / Jared —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Procurement path options we discussed:
   - Marketplace (preferred by us for simple procurement + consolidated billing)
   - Customer PO / vendor invoice (standard net-30 or net-45)
   - Credit card (one-time or corporate card)

2) Your stated constraints:
   - ACME finance noted a preference for POs for purchases > $50k/year
   - There may be an internal policy that blocks vendor POs for new SaaS vendors unless an exception is approved

3) Asks from Redwood:
   - Can you confirm whether ACME will accept vendor invoices/POs for Redwood (we can supply W-9 and vendor setup info)?
   - If POs are blocked, would ACME consider purchasing via AWS/Azure marketplace (we are listed) or via corporate card for initial pilot?
   - Any required paperwork for a PO exception (procurement form, finance approval) — if you can share the template, we’ll fill it out ASAP.

Attached: Redwood_CTA_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW), redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx (estimate)

Proposed next step: If policy requires an exception, Ben to work with Redwood Sales Ops + Marissa to submit an exception request and provide the documentation needed by finance. If marketplace is acceptable, we’ll share the marketplace SKU and a one-page procurement note.

Thanks — I’ll follow up on Monday to check status.

Best,
Ben Carter

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement path & PO details (ACME)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from procurement/finance: 

- ACME generally requires a PO for contractual spend > $50k annually. For small pilots under that threshold, procurement often allows purchasing via corporate card, but our vendor onboarding policy is stricter: new vendors must be set up in the vendor system before we can issue a PO.
- There is a known blocker for SaaS vendors without a tax form or verified vendor ID — that’s why vendor setup is the first step.
- If vendor setup will take too long, we can consider marketplace purchase (AWS Marketplace) if the SKU and billing party meet our requirements. Marketplace purchases go through our cloud procurement and typically do not require vendor setup in the same way.

We do not have an explicit ‘no PO’ policy — more of a vendor onboarding gating. I’ll loop in procurement to confirm the exact documents required (W-9/equivalent, vendor profile, contact for invoices). I’ve cc'd procurement and Jared (finance) to this thread.

Samantha Lee
Head of Strategic Procurement, ACME
Samantha.Lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Procurement path & PO details (ACME)

Ben / Rishi —

Follow-up guidance from Sales Ops for this exact scenario: 

- If customer procurement requires vendor setup and PO for >$50k, we should: 1) provide vendor paperwork (W-9, vendor onboarding packet) 2) offer a short pilot via credit card or marketplace while vendor setup is pending 3) submit a procurement-exception request if the customer cannot accept marketplace or card.
- I attached our procurement-exception-template.docx (simple form Procurement teams often accept) and a one-page marketplace procurement note we can send to ACME.
- Rishi: can you advise whether Finance will accept a prepaid invoice (we can invoice for a 3-month prepay) as an alternative? That sometimes avoids a PO barrier.

If ACME confirms vendor setup is required, we’ll prepare vendor paperwork and a formal exception request and send it to Samantha + procurement. I can draft the exception request this afternoon if that helps.

-Marissa
Director, Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement path & PO details (ACME)

Thanks Samantha — appreciate the clarity. Proposed commercial paths so we can move quickly: 

Option A (fastest): Marketplace purchase (AWS Marketplace). We’ll provide SKU and one-page PO note. You can provision through cloud procurement and billing will show on ACME cloud bill. No vendor setup required in many cases.

Option B: Corporate card for pilot < $50k. We can accept a credit card payment to start pilot immediately, then transition to PO/vendor invoice for scale.

Option C: Vendor invoice with vendor onboarding + PO. If you need this path, we’ll immediately submit W-9 and vendor profile and can also offer a 3-month prepay invoice to speed approval (Finance note: see HubSpot deal for terms).

Next steps I suggest: please confirm whether marketplace is acceptable as a short-term path. If not, let us know the vendor onboarding checklist and we’ll submit the docs today. If procurement needs an exception form completed, we’ll use the attached template (procurement-exception-template.docx) and have Sales Ops lead the submission.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/ACME-4572 (tracking + SOW attached)

Best,
Ben

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks — I’ve escalated to procurement and finance. They confirmed the vendor onboarding checklist and requested: W-9, vendor contact, bank info (for ACH), and a short vendor justification memo. They also said marketplace is acceptable for the pilot — please send the SKU + billing party name and we’ll evaluate.

Procurement opened a ticket for an exception if vendor onboarding cannot be completed in time: https://acme.procurement.example.com/portal/ticket/7890. They asked that any exception requests be accompanied by the vendor justification memo (one paragraph), expected spend, and the contact in finance who will sponsor.

I’ll get back with timing but marketplace looks like the fastest route.

Samantha
